application_guidance.input_pattern: A proof contains <∇ψ(b)−∇ψ(a),c−a> with Bregman terms defined in the same orientation.
read_original_when: Changing to extended-valued ψ, infinite-dimensional spaces, generalized derivatives or different Bregman orientations.
sensitive_conditions: The second argument of each Bregman term is a differentiability point.
Nonnegativity is a separate convexity property, not a consequence of the identity.

content.intended_use: Establish the algebraic identity used in the SANP one-step estimate.

proofs.full_local_argument: All terms are defined because a,b∈S and c∈closure(S). Expanding the left side gives [ψ(c)−ψ(a)−<∇ψ(a),c−a>]+[ψ(a)−ψ(b)−<∇ψ(b),a−b>]−[ψ(c)−ψ(b)−<∇ψ(b),c−b>]. The six function values cancel. The remaining expression is −<∇ψ(a),c−a>+<∇ψ(b),(c−b)−(a−b)>=<∇ψ(b)−∇ψ(a),c−a>. This proves the identity for every stated triple, including c on the boundary; no derivative at c is used.
proofs.locator: Source statement: printed p.171 / PDF p.5, Lemma 4.1, (4.14). The following argument is a local reconstruction, not quoted source text.
map: Expand the three definitions and cancel finite ψ values.
proofs.reading_coverage: Actually viewed and read Lemma 4.1 and (4.14) on original-page derivative PDF p.5; checked Bψ definition on PDF p.4. Source attributes the lemma to Chen and Teboulle [5]; that earlier paper was not read or used as a separate dependency.

assumptions: a,b∈S and c∈closure(S). ψ has finite real values on closure(S).
No convexity or strong convexity is needed for this identity; without convexity it does not imply Bψ≥0.
statement.objects_and_definitions: For n≥1 let S⊂R^n be open and ψ:closure(S)→R be continuously differentiable on S. For u∈closure(S), v∈S define Bψ(u,v)=ψ(u)−ψ(v)−<∇ψ(v),u−v>.
statement.parameter_domains: Every integer n≥1; no stepsize or oracle parameter.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For every such S, ψ, a, b and c; deterministic pointwise identity.
